clue.text: Old European line for 15

definitions.note: 15 across is DRESSER, here a fashion designer, one who dresses people

parts.note: a Gaul was an inhabitant of ancient Gaul
a tier is a row or line, as of seats

explanation.surface: An ancient continental standing in for someone, like a substitute in a line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' points at the solution of 15 across, read as a fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Paul Gaultier is a French fashion designer, so he dresses people for a living.

clue.text: See 24 across
Brick dropped on head of raging foreman

indicators.note: on places one piece after the other in this down clue

parts.note: to drop a brick is British slang for making a blunder, a gaffe

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of raging is used

explanation.surface: A brick falls on an angry site boss's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brick dropped' is the British idiom for a social blunder, not a building mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is British slang for a boss or works foreman.

clue.text: Pen capturing the Guardian's spirit

indicators.note: a pen capturing something holds it within, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: a pen for animals is an enclosure, a cage
the Guardian speaking of itself says our

explanation.surface: An enclosure locks up the newspaper's spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters in the Guardian use 'the Guardian's' for OUR, as the paper's own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit in the sense of pluck or bravery is a synonym of courage.

clue.text: Mint carrying starter of quality, a kind of light dish

indicators.note: a coin carrying things holds them in its middle

parts.note: mint suggests coinage, here a coin

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: UV is ultraviolet light

explanation.surface: A cook offers a quality, light, minty dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a kind of light dish' looks like one phrase; the definition is just 'dish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coq au vin is a French chicken stew cooked in red wine.

clue.text: Still without a Poet Laureate?

parts.note: Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009
less means lacking or without, as in 'penniless'

explanation.surface: Is the country still without an official national poet?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words to see the poet lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is not moving at all, entirely stationary.

clue.text: Brief assault with hard stick

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an assault is an attack
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A short attack made with a solid stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a weapon noun; it is the verb meaning fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick one thing to another is to fasten or fix it on.

clue.text: Liqueur in 15

definitions.meaning: John ... is a fashion designer, a dresser of people

explanation.surface: A drink served in a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are proper names: the Italian drink and the British couturier John Galliano.

clue.text: Round window beginning to open in European city

parts.note: a round shape is O
a port is a ship's window, a porthole

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A circular window starts to open onto a continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, the Portuguese port city.

clue.text: Friend friendly, though not originally

indicators.note: without its original, first letter

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly

explanation.surface: A friend who is friendly, though not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or partner, a friend in a cause.

clue.text: Jersey, say, female 15 put on chap, unfinished

indicators.note: the designer is put on, before, the chap

parts.note: Giorgio Armani, the fashion designer, a dresser

indicators.note: an unfinished word has not reached its end, so the chap's final letter is left off

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: A woman wears a Jersey made by a designer on a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like a knitted top, apt beside a designer; it is the dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, an example of livestock.

clue.text: One in form again after tossing over sausage

indicators.note: one is placed in the other piece
tossing a word over flips it end to end

parts.note: to renew is to form again
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone reshapes a sausage after flipping it over in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiener is the American name for a frankfurter, a type of sausage.

clue.text: Love essentially is ending, unfortunately, sinking very fast

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone awry, so the letters are mixed
the essence of a word is its middle, the letters inside its ends

explanation.surface: Love is ending sadly, with things sinking fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes OV from Love; with IS and ENDING it is rearranged as 'unfortunately' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep plunge, so diving this way means falling very fast.

clue.text: 15 presented with an award before day's end

indicators.note: places the award before the next piece

parts.note: presented means given
CH is Companion of Honour, a British award

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dresser receives an award late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubert de Givenchy was a French fashion designer, who dressed Audrey Hepburn.

clue.text: Furniture item fool perhaps shortened to get round corner, finally

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the extra letter
a pudding word shortened is cut short at the tail, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, an example of dessert

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool shortens his route round a corner past a sideboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit and cream, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a sideboard or cabinet with shelves for dishes.

clue.text: Bully lingered in ring, once

indicators.note: bully means push around, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A thug hung about in a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: To engirdle is an old word for encircle, to surround like a girdle.

clue.text: All over the place, drunk, empty bottles

indicators.note: the words bottle the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A drunk is a mess with empty bottles everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy, dishevelled hair or clothing is all over the place.

clue.text: 15 with a cut sent up, still

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means written from bottom to top

parts.note: Christian Dior, the fashion designer, a dresser
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: A designer's work is cut and mocked, yet things stay still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is a noun: a single photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A Polaroid is an instant photograph, a still image.

clue.text: Two legs acting?

parts.note: ON is the leg side in cricket and STAGE is a leg of a journey; together they mean performing

explanation.surface: A pair of legs is performing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's leg side is also called the on side, so ON is one leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor performing in a play is up in front of the audience.

clue.text: Garment: gear regularly kept in 15

indicators.note: one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: Pierre Cardin, the fashion designer, a dresser

indicators.note: every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A garment's gear is regularly stored in a dresser.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket that buttons up the front.

clue.text: A gentle land

parts.note: a light touch is a gentle one

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a soft landing.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to come down and settle, as a bird lands.

clue.text: Wine has run out for curry dish

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Marsala is a fortified Sicilian wine
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The wine has run out, so there is curry to drink with.
explanation.definitionFit: A masala is a spiced dish or spice blend from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Dealer in fine textiles, Queen impressed by a Scottish version of herself?

indicators.note: the Queen is pressed into the next piece

parts.note: Mc in Scottish surnames means son of
ER, Elizabeth Regina
the Queen herself is ER

explanation.surface: A cloth merchant meets a Queen and her Scottish double.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scottish version of the Queen is imagined as a Mc surname, as in MacDonald; the real Queen is pressed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercer is a trader in silks, velvets and other costly cloths.

clue.text: US medal Jack stuck on old US comedian

indicators.note: the sailor is stuck on the end of the comedian

parts.note: Phil Silvers, star of the TV show Bilko
jack tar is slang for a sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: A sailor is pinned with an award beside a veteran comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Silver Star is the third-highest American military decoration for gallantry.

clue.text: Lead lost in fencing, is that my sport?

indicators.note: the lead, or first letter, is lost

parts.note: fencing is the sport of swordplay

explanation.surface: A fencer losing the lead wonders if this sport is for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my sport' is the setter speaking: a cryptic setter's game is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Puns and clever manipulation of letters are the setter's own game.

clue.text: Reportedly, I didn't catch that old mechanical engineer

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: what? is said when you failed to hear

explanation.surface: Someone mishears the name of a historic engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the question word and the surname sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine.

clue.text: 15's artery leaving heart

definitions.note: 's stands for is: the designer Coco Chanel is a dresser

indicators.note: the heart, a middle letter, leaves

parts.note: an artery is a channel, a main route

explanation.surface: A cabinet's artery runs away from the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco Chanel was the French couturier who founded the House of Chanel.

clue.text: Winger gets it on target, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly marks an unexpected order of the letters

explanation.surface: A football winger gets the ball on target, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a common European songbird, and birds have wings.
